xaendarPlugin.summary: Creates the Vite plugin that compiles the templates and the stylesheets of the components ahead of time, and type-checks the project.
xaendarPlugin.description:
The plugin, named xaendar, goes in the plugins of the Vite configuration, after the transform of the standard decorators. The xd CLI adds it on its own, with the options read from xaendar.json. The options are described below; their type is XaendarPluginOptions.

For every component declared in a file ending with .xd.component.ts, the plugin reads the options of @WebComponent from the source code, validates and claims the selector, type-checks the template against the class, and adds to the module the imports of two virtual modules: the render function compiled from the template, and the CSSStyleSheet built from the stylesheet. A template or a stylesheet shared by several components is compiled once, into a module they all import. A @WebComponent in a TypeScript file with another name is an error.

Vite only strips the types, so the plugin checks them: a build type-checks the whole project once it ends, as tsc --noEmit does, and the dev server checks each TypeScript file as it serves it. The compiler options, strict ones included, come from the tsconfig.json of the directory Vite is started from, or of the nearest directory above it holding one: start Vite from the root of the project.

In the dev server, the plugin watches what each component depends on: its template, its stylesheet, the components its template imports, the classes it extends and the files its type check reads. Editing any of them compiles the component again.

members.customElements:
The patterns of the tag names of the custom elements of other libraries, such as Shoelace or an element written without Xaendar, which the templates use without importing them. In a pattern, * stands for any sequence of characters, and every other character stands for itself: sl-* matches sl-button and sl-icon-button, vanilla-stars only itself. A pattern must match the whole tag name.

Defaults to none: every tag with a hyphen used by a template must then be a component imported by it with @import, or the build fails. The CLI passes the customElements of xaendar.json.

The compiler treats a matching tag as a native element: its bindings write attributes, so the element receives strings, its attributes are not checked against any class, and $event has the type HTMLElementEventMap declares for the event, any for an event it does not declare. The library still has to define the element at run time. A tag that matches a pattern and is also a component imported by the template fails the build: keep the patterns specific to the other libraries. See Selectors and registration.

configuration.title: Adding it to the Vite configuration
configuration.body: A project driving Vite directly lists the plugin after the Babel transform of the standard decorators: the plugin adds its registration before the static block Babel generates in each decorated class. In the opposite order, every component fails with the error below.

cli.title: Projects run by the CLI
cli.body: xd start, xd build and xd test add Babel and the plugin to the configuration of vite.config.ts on their own, so the configuration does not list them. The CLI passes to the plugin the customElements of the xaendar.json found in the directory it is run from, none when the file or the field is missing.

errors.title: Reading the errors
errors.body: The messages of the plugin start with Xaendar:, and the ones of the type check with [TypeChecker], followed by the position in the template and the excerpt involved. A component that cannot be compiled fails the build; in the dev server it is left without its render function, and throws when it is connected. A TypeScript file with type errors is not served, and its errors show in the Vite overlay too. The Error encyclopedia lists the messages.

styles.title: Stylesheets
styles.body: A stylesheet can be a .css, .scss, .sass or .less file: any other extension fails to compile. Sass and Less files are compiled with the sass and less packages, optional peer dependencies that the project installs itself, and their imports are resolved at build time. Comments are then removed, and in vite build the CSS is also minified with Lightning CSS, unless build.cssMinify is false. Each file becomes one CSSStyleSheet, adopted by every component pointing to it. See Styling.

XaendarPluginOptions.summary: The type of the options of xaendarPlugin().
XaendarPluginOptions.description: The object passed to xaendarPlugin(), whose page describes each option. Every option is optional: xaendarPlugin() without arguments takes the defaults.

members.customElements: The patterns of the tag names of the custom elements of other libraries, such as sl-*, which the templates use like native elements. Defaults to none. See xaendarPlugin() for the syntax of the patterns and how the compiler treats the tags matching them.
